TODAY I still struggle to understand why Trump, even as a billionaire, continues to maintain habits like this. What if I told you that the billionaire President of the United States does something every single morning that he refuses to allow ANYONE else to do for him — a tradition his father taught him more than 60 years ago, and the reason behind it carries a powerful lesson about what TRUE character really means?
For over 60 YEARS, Donald Trump has reportedly polished his own shoes every morning.
Not his staff. Not hotel workers. Not professional shoe polishers.
TRUMP himself.
With his own hands. His own polish. His own time.
White House staff have reportedly offered on numerous occasions:
“Mr. President, we can take care of polishing your shoes.”
Trump’s response has always been:
“NO. My father taught me when I was a young boy: A man polishes his own shoes. It builds CHARACTER. It reminds you that no matter how successful you become, you should never think you are above basic discipline.”
Think about that.
Trump has reportedly maintained this shoe-polishing routine since his childhood in the 1950s.
Throughout the building of his business empire.
Throughout becoming a billionaire.
Throughout becoming PRESIDENT.
Still.
Every.
Morning.
He polishes his own shoes.
Staff members have reportedly seen this routine: Trump wakes up, and before important meetings, presidential briefings, and the responsibilities of running the country — he sits down with his shoe polish and brush and takes care of his own formal footwear.
“My father said: ‘The day you become too important to polish your own shoes is the day you lose your character.’ I never forgot that.”
For over SIX DECADES, Trump has reportedly continued to practice the lesson his father taught him.
More than 60 YEARS of everyday discipline that nobody photographs, nobody applauds, and something most people might never even know about.
Simply a son remembering a promise he made to his father:
“I will never become too important to do this myself.”
Here's the lesson this teaches us:
True character isn't built during the biggest moments of life — it develops through the small daily disciplines you follow for DECADES, even when nobody is watching.
👞🇺🇲 Drop 👞 if Trump's reported 60-year discipline motivates you.
Comment: What lesson did YOUR father or mother teach you that you continue to follow even today?
Share this so others can understand:
Character = daily habits.
Follow if you believe the lessons our parents teach us can become lifelong promises.
Trump's shoe polishing = a 60-year promise! 👞🙏🇺🇲

🇮🇷🇺🇸 Trump wants out of the Iran war... Netanyahu’s cabinet reportedly just told the military to get ready for more

Amir Handjani, a Quincy Institute board member, has no doubt Trump wants out, and he says the one thing that can wreck it is Israel striking first and Washington feeling it has to join in.

That would be the third time Iran got hit in the middle of talks.

Amir says Tehran is far more prepared than it was in February and has already said it will fire past the region at any European base that supports the strikes.

He thinks a deal is coming either way, which leaves one open question:

“Are we going to have another war before we get the deal?”

Amir leans no, because Netanyahu’s likely replacement is more measured on Iran.

The risk is whatever Netanyahu does before he leaves.

@ahandjani  @WeTheBrandon

🇺🇸🇮🇷 Is Trump's "status quo" on Iran an exit... or the on-ramp back to war?

Andrew Day, senior editor at The American Conservative, says the blockade and sanctions plan sold to Trump as a middle path can’t hold still, because it’s built to squeeze Iran harder every week and Tehran won’t sit through that forever.

He adds that Iran has about 1,700 ballistic missiles and builds roughly 50 a month, more than the US makes in Patriot interceptors in a year.

Clint Russell, host of Liberty Lockdown, argues there’s no clean exit left, since Iran now has to answer any strike and Israel can restart the war by moving first.

They also get into whether one big strike could let Washington walk away and what Democrats do with their new majority.

Every week the squeeze continues without a deal, the odds of Iran or Israel forcing the next round go up, and America’s interceptor stock isn’t keeping pace.
